name: LLaDA-8B-Instruct
attention_variant: full bidirectional attention, no causal mask
notes: Diffusion language model, not an autoregressive one. config.json: model_type 'llada', architectures ['LLaDAModelLM'], d_model 4096, n_layers 32, n_heads 32, n_kv_heads 32, max_sequence_length 4096, block_type 'llama'. Crucially use_cache is false and there is no KV-cache machinery at all - the config has no sliding_window, no num_key_value_heads distinction worth noting (32/32), and the README states generation works by iteratively unmasking tokens. kv_cache_bytes_per_token = 0, but NOT because memory is flat: there is no autoregressive KV cache because the model never generates token-by-token. Each denoising step runs a full bidirectional forward pass over the entire sequence, so the cost per generated token is (number of denoising steps) x (one full-sequence forward pass), and compute scales with sequence length x steps rather than with a growing cache. This makes the workload compute-bound in a way autoregressive serving is not, and it is why llama.cpp/vLLM KV-cache management has nothing to contribute here. gqa_ratio = 1 (32 heads, 32 KV heads). head_dim derived as 4096 / 32 = 128. active_params_b equals params_b because every weight participates in every denoising step. Practical caveat: custom modeling code (modeling_llada.py) is required, and vLLM support is via a separate diffusion-LM path rather than the normal causal-LM path. context_scaling is null: context length is native to the pretrained config, no rope_scaling.
